case.pattern_description: Under-threshold burst: 4 online purchases each between $450 and $499.99 ($1,906.07 in total) inside 30 minutes on a card with almost no online history, split across 2 New device profiles and 2 purchaser email domains. Amounts sit just under a $500 authorisation threshold. 12 other cards show the identical shape within 30 days (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06208-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2); five closed cases with this shape were confirmed as undocumented fraud and reported.

evidence.claim: Customer C07297 denies making the $482.12 purchase 3476682, stating 'I never made this $482.12 purchase'; in this bank's history 4,665 of 4,665 customer-reported closed cases were confirmed fraud and none were cleared.

under_threshold_burst on card C07297-K1 found a 4-member online burst (3476602 $478.95, 3476633 $456.96, 3476665 $488.04, 3476682 $482.12), all between $450 and $499.99, spanning 20:00 to 20:30 on 2016-11-21 (30 minutes), alternating between device profiles Trident/7.0|Windows 7|ie 11.0 for desktop|1920x1080 and iOS Device|iOS 11.2.1|mobile safari 11.0|2208x1242 and between billing regions 264.0 and 476.0.

As of opening this card had 199 prior transactions (card_seq 200 - 1) with a prior median amount of $62.93 and a prior maximum of $1,104; only 4 of its prior 30-day transactions were online (card_profile.last30.n_online=4), so a run of 4 online purchases in one 30-minute window is a sharp departure from its baseline.

find_similar_cases returned three closed cases with the same-device overlap reason that were confirmed fraud near this amount band: CC-3624 ($449.89, card_not_present_new_device), CC-1476 ($499.89, card_not_present_fraud), and CC-1960 ($461.87, account_takeover).

evidence.claim: recurring_charge_check on 3476682 found only 1 matching prior purchase (total_n=1) at this amount/product/place, so the R7 recurring-pattern exception (which requires >=5 prior matches) does not apply and the denial routes to R2.

The case-memory calibrated score (cms_p) on the flagged transaction is 0.0126, and on the two non-flagged burst members it is 0.0864-0.0877, both far below the floored probability, showing the memory family reads this transaction as low-risk in isolation.

The device profile 'Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080' is used by 543 cards all-time and 359 cards in the 30 days before opening and is not strong (is_strong=false), so under the strength rule it does not itself count as shared-origin (R6) evidence despite 6 associated fraud cases.

case.summary: Verdict fraud, probability 0.90. The pattern is an under-threshold burst: four online purchases of $456.96-$488.04 (each just under $500) within 30 minutes on 2016-11-21, alternating two device profiles and two regions, exposure $1,906.07 across transactions 3476602, 3476633, 3476665 and 3476682. Decisive facts: the customer's denial of 3476682 and the same burst shape recurring on 12 other cards with prior confirmed-fraud precedent, despite low cms_p on these transactions in isolation. No evidence request was needed; recommending BLOCK_CARD (L1) and FILE_REPORT (L2), pending approval, alongside CREATE_CASE and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST.

sar.narrative: This report is filed under internal case AC-HHG-006 to describe an undocumented coordinated fraud pattern, an under-threshold burst of online purchases, identified on card C07297-K1. The customer is C07297, a debit mastercard cardholder with a single card on file; the activity involves two device profiles, "Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080" and "iOS Device | iOS 11.2.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2208x1242", and no other card was found connected to this card's activity. The case was opened 2016-11-22 after the customer stated the charge was not made, denying transaction 3476682. On 2016-11-21 four online purchases were made in rapid succession: at 20:00, $478.95 (transaction 3476602) in billing region 264.0 on the Trident/Windows device flagged as a new device; at 20:10, $456.96 (transaction 3476633) in billing region 476.0 on the iOS Safari device, also flagged as new; at 20:24, $488.04 (transaction 3476665) again in region 476.0 on the same iOS device; and at 20:30, $482.12 (transaction 3476682, the disputed charge) again in region 264.0 on the Trident device, for total exposure of $1,906.07. All four amounts fall in the $450 to $499.99 band, just under a $500 authorization threshold, and the purchases alternated between the two device profiles and two regions within a 30-minute span. Twelve other cards (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06208-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1 and C12641-K2) show the identical shape of four online purchases each between $450 and $499.99 within a short window in the surrounding 30 days, and five closed cases with this same shape were previously confirmed as undocumented fraud and reported, indicating a repeated, coordinated pattern rather than an isolated incident on this card. This activity is inconsistent with the cardholder's history as of the case opening: in the 199 prior transactions on this card, the median amount was $62.93 and the maximum was $1,104.00, only 4 of the prior 30 days' transactions were online, and the account was overwhelmingly used in person in regions 264.0, 191.0 and 485.0; a cluster of four online purchases near $500 each, using two different device profiles within 30 minutes, has no precedent in that baseline. No prior suspicious activity report has been filed on this card, and no prior report was found for the device profiles or any connected card; OFAC screening of the customer and card identifiers against the SDN list returned no match. A case has been opened and the matter escalated to an analyst for review of the wider wave of similarly shaped activity; a block of card C07297-K1 is recommended and awaits team-lead approval, and this filing itself is recommended and awaits fraud-manager approval, covering total suspicious activity of $1,906.07 across transactions 3476602, 3476633, 3476665 and 3476682.
